messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed during the maintenance window last night the eu-west-1 GPU pool has NO audit logs between 02:14-02:32 UTC. KMS key access events missing as well. Anyone else see this?

tj: I'm seeing a spike of failed provisioning jobs around that time, autoscaler retried ~6x. Could be related. :thinking_face: 

kai: quick check shows the flow logs for subnet prod-eu-gpu-1 were disabled at ~02:10. Cloud console shows 'Flow log: disabled' and the timeline matches. Tried: `aws ec2 describe-flow-logs --filter Name=resource-id,Values=subnet-abcdef12`

maria: who toggled flow logs? We have terraform guardrails, but drift happens. @nisha did any of the private-deploy test moves touch that subnet?

nisha: yeah — I moved that subnet into the new private VPC peer for the on-prem test earlier that day. I created a temporary firewall rule to allow debug egress to the logging endpoint and might have toggled flow logs while testing. :grimacing: I'll open a revert PR now.

alex: also noticed the KMS automated rotation job ran at 02:11. CloudTrail shows multiple 'AccessDenied' errors for the infra-agent principal trying to decrypt. Sample CloudTrail snippet I grabbed: 
```
Error: AccessDenied
principal: infra-agent@redwood-infra
action: kms:Decrypt
resource: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:999999999999:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```

tj: so two coincident issues — flow logs off and KMS denies. That explains missing VPC-level traffic logs, but why are CloudTrail KMS events missing entirely? CloudTrail should still record the management events.

kai: CloudTrail events for that timeframe are incomplete. The S3 delivery logs show a bunch of PutObject failures around 02:12: `NoSuchKey`/`AccessDenied` on the partitioned path. Looks like CloudTrail couldn't write to the S3 prefix because the bucket policy denies the delivery role.

nisha: ack — I recently tightened the org bucket policy to deny non-TLS and only allow specific principals. I probably omitted the CloudTrail delivery role when I updated the policy. That would block PutObject from the delivery account.

maria: This is a compliance risk — missing audit logs for critical GPU infra + KMS DENY during maintenance. Action items: restore logs, ensure CT delivery, verify KMS key policy, and confirm no customer data exposure.

alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) re-enable flow logs on prod-eu-gpu-1, 2) add CloudTrail delivery role to S3 bucket policy, 3) patch KMS key policy to include infra-agent principal. I'll open an emergency terraform PR with the minimal diffs. Example patch: 
```hcl
resource "aws_flow_log" "prod_eu_gpu_1" {
  subnet_id = "subnet-abcdef12"
  traffic_type = "ALL"
  log_destination = aws_s3_bucket.vpc_flow_logs.arn
}

resource "aws_s3_bucket_policy" "audit_bucket" {
  bucket = aws_s3_bucket.audit.id
  policy = jsonencode({
    Statement = [
      { Effect = "Allow", Principal = { AWS = "arn:aws:iam::cloudtrail-delivery:role/CloudTrailDelivery" }, Action = "s3:PutObject", Resource = "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-cloudtrail/*" }
    ]
  })
}
```

deploy-bot: deploy request #9876 queued by alex — plan shows +1 flow log resource and bucket policy update. :rocket:

tj: cost note: enabling flow logs will add roughly 4–6GB/day for that subnet (ingress+egress). Rough estimate ~ $0.10/GB -> ~ $12–18/month per subnet. Suggest lifecycle policy to compress/transition to Glacier/Archive after 30 days.

kai: additional root cause: provisioning failures also seen because the subnet had low available IPs — autoscaler couldn't attach new nodes. We should monitor free IPs and alert at 20% threshold. Sample CloudWatch math: `free_ips = cidr_size - used_ips` and alert when free_ips / cidr_size < 0.2.

nisha: I'll remove the deny from the bucket policy and add the CloudTrail delivery role, and patch the KMS key policy to include `arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/infra-agent`. Will tag the PR with `pg-incident` and request fast review.

maria: thanks. Follow-up: we need a short retro to capture the process gap — moving subnets into test VPC should NOT disable logging. @sre-oncall can you schedule a 30min postmortem and include runbooks for flow logs and S3 CT policy checks?

sre-oncall: on it — booking a 30min sync, will include the runbook and add an automated check (monitor CloudTrail PutObject success per region + verify flow log enabled for all gpu subnets). Sending calendar invite now.

alex: once logs backfill we'll confirm audit completeness. Also filing a ticket to evaluate reserved capacity for critical GPU pools to avoid provisioning fallbacks during maintenance — weighing cost vs availability.

maria: great. Keep updates in this thread and paste PR links when available.
